purpose: Teach: 青色/千代田/吉野/鹿島/ミシェル/帯広/朝日新聞社/小学館

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが青色の作業着で働かれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to work in that blue uniform.
lines.style: Soft, reaching back into memory. Gentle nostalgia without sadness. Speaking as though tracing the outline of an old photograph with his finger.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、千代田区の本社に通われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — and your grandfather commuted to the Chiyoda headquarters every day, didn't he?
lines.style: Warm, patient correction. Not contradicting, just gently steering toward her own memory. A small smile in the voice — she knows what he was doing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが吉野山の桜を見に行かれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he went to see the cherry blossoms at Yoshino.
lines.style: Same gentle reaching. The rhythm of remembering together. A quiet pause after the image, as though letting it settle.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、鹿島神宮を参拝されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather visited Kashima Shrine, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warmly insistent now. Still tender, but there's a pattern she's following — a gentle, playful persistence. The lilt of someone who has done this dance before.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがミシェル先生の論文を翻訳された
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he translated a paper for Professor Michel.
lines.style: The same wistful cadence, but quieter now. Slower pace. As though the memory is becoming fainter, more precious for being harder to reach.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、帯広の親戚を訪ねられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather visited relatives in Obihiro, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Still warm, but there's a gentleness underneath now — as though she's noticing something shifting. Her voice remains clear, but with a quality of tender attention.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが朝日新聞社にお勤めだった
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he worked at the Asahi Shimbun.
lines.style: Slower still. Each word has weight. The wistfulness has deepened into something more fragile. He's holding onto these moments.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、小学館の児童誌を孫に買って下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather bought children's magazines from Shogakukan for the grandchildren, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Her voice is softer now, reaching toward him with something unspoken. A tenderness that knows what he's doing. Close, intimate, like a hand held in the dark.
